account.definition: The post-auth standing arc a client moves through — unregistered, unverified, verified — scoped by actor and managed by the account composable.

auth.definition: Unified authentication for guest, client, and staff actors — login, registration, and session establishment, handled by the auth composable.

basket.definition: The customer's in-progress order — the collection of products, billing cycles, promotions, and currency selected before checkout. The headless basket is the reactive source of truth the storefront app reads and mutates.

billing.definition: The billing details attached to a basket — validating, updating, and clearing them, and observing the billing lifecycle's state transitions — managed by the basket billing composable.

brand.definition: The white-labelled organisation a storefront runs as — its settings, configuration values, and enabled modules, fetched and unified by the brand composable.

cart.definition: The Vue.js storefront app (`apps/cart`) that renders the customer-facing basket and checkout UI. It is a consumer of the headless business logic and the client-vue integration layer, not the basket concept itself — see the package-layer split in ADR-007.

client.definition: The authenticated customer's profile and account standing — identity, contact details, and the account-lifecycle state (unregistered, unverified, verified) layered on top of it.

currency.definition: The currency a basket is priced and displayed in. Changing the basket currency re-prices every line item; the selection is managed by the basket currency composable.

custom-field.definition: A brand-configured question attached to clients — its definition (code, type, required/visibility rules) is shared across every client on the brand; only the value differs per client. Definitions and their value semantics (per-type coercion, schema/form generation, the image-upload flow for the IMAGE type) are read through the client custom fields composables; a specific client's own values live on that client's personal details.

domain.definition: A domain-name product — searched for availability, registered or transferred, and configured as part of an order. Domain search and lifecycle are handled by the domain composable.

feedback.definition: User-facing messages — errors, successes, warnings, and system notifications — added, dismissed, and displayed through a global feedback state machine.

invoice.definition: The billable document raised for an order — client, currency, line items, payment history, and the paid/unpaid amount summary. Invoice data is loaded and invalidated by the invoice composable.

order.definition: The invoice-payment lifecycle a basket converts into at checkout — orchestrated by the order machine, which spawns the payment-detail actor and drives retry and partial-payment loops until the invoice is settled.

payment.definition: The state, context, and actions that orchestrate a single payment attempt against a gateway — meta-information, error handling, and the pay/refresh event triggers, driven by the payment composable's state machine.

payment-gateway.definition: A provider integration (Stripe, PayPal, and others) that authorises and captures payment for an order. Gateways are abstracted behind a common interface so the checkout flow is provider-agnostic.

personal-details.definition: A client's own profile record — native fields (first name, last name, public name, interface language) plus the client's own custom field values — read and edited through a diff-only save. Distinct from the custom field definitions and value semantics it consumes, which are owned by the client custom fields composables.

product.definition: A sellable item in a brand's catalogue — hosting plans, domains, add-ons — with its pricing, billing cycles, and configuration options. Products are browsed via the catalogue and added to the basket.

promotion.definition: A discount or offer applied to a basket, typically via a promo code, that adjusts line-item or order totals. Promotions are validated and applied through the basket promotions composable.

query.definition: The TanStack Query layer that fetches, caches, and invalidates server data behind every composable. Query keys and the shared query client are exposed through the query composable.

recommendations.definition: Suggested products surfaced from the recommendation engine — either scoped to a specific product (for product-detail or post-add-to-basket upsell) or fetched generally — via the recommendations composables.

routing.definition: Route management, navigation, and flow control across the storefront — integrating internationalisation, session, and basket state to resolve routes and drive funnel progression.

scope.definition: The keyed registry mechanism that gives each composable instance an isolated, reusable footprint so multiple baskets or products can coexist on one page without sharing state. Scope keys namespace every module's reactive state.

session.definition: The authenticated (or guest) context a basket and its actions run within, including the current client, brand, and access tokens. Session state is coordinated by the session composable and its state machine.

system.definition: Brand-agnostic reference data (countries, currencies, statuses, billing cycles, ticket departments, and similar lookups) exposed through the system composable.

theming.definition: The per-brand visual configuration (colours, typography, layout tokens) that lets one headless codebase render many branded storefronts. Theme values are resolved by the theming composable.

@upmind-automation/headless!ACCOUNT_SCOP.name: ACCOUNT_SCOPE_MATRIX
@upmind-automation/headless!ACCOUNT_SCOP.tsdoc:
Account module scope matrix (runtime value - single source of truth).
Mirrors AUTH_SCOPE_MATRIX shape — actor-agnostic standing/verification.
- staff: can act on behalf of 'client'
- client: acts as self only
- guest: valid scope but not actionable (no account standing)

@upmind-automation/headless!ADDRESS_TYPE.name: ADDRESS_TYPE_KEYS
@upmind-automation/headless!ADDRESS_TYPE.tsdoc:
A constant object mapping human-readable names to their corresponding numeric keys
from the AddressTypes array. This provides a type-safe way to reference
address types in code.

@upmind-automation/headless!AUTH_SCOPE_M.name: AUTH_SCOPE_MATRIX
@upmind-automation/headless!AUTH_SCOPE_M.tsdoc:
Auth module scope matrix (runtime value - single source of truth).
Defines which actors can operate on which contexts.
- staff: can act on behalf of 'client'
- client: acts as self only (null)
- guest: valid scope but not actionable (can only view, not switch to)

@upmind-automation/headless!AUTH_SESSION.name: AUTH_SESSION_QUERY_KEY_BASE
@upmind-automation/headless!AUTH_SESSION.tsdoc:
Shared query key base - used for invalidation across all scopes.
Individual services extend this with scope-specific segments.

@upmind-automation/headless!AccountConte.name: AccountContextTypes
@upmind-automation/headless!AccountConte.tsdoc:
Context types for account module.
Defines what entities a staff member can manage account standing on behalf of.

@upmind-automation/headless!AccountScope.name: AccountScopeMatrix
@upmind-automation/headless!AccountScope.tsdoc: Account module scope matrix type (derived from runtime const).

@upmind-automation/headless!ActorContext.name: ActorContextMatrix
@upmind-automation/headless!ActorContext.tsdoc:
Actor-to-context matrix type.
Each module defines which contexts are valid for each actor.
Context types are defined by the module itself (typically as an enum).

Note: SELF is included in the matrix but should map to `never` since
it's resolved to a concrete actor at runtime before context lookup.

@upmind-automation/headless!Address.name: Address
@upmind-automation/headless!Address.tsdoc:
Interface representing a comprehensive address object, extending AddressModel
with additional identifiers, contextual information, and meta-data about the address.
This is typically used for addresses retrieved from the API or displayed in the UI.

@upmind-automation/headless!AddressConte.name: AddressContext
@upmind-automation/headless!AddressConte.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for address management within a client item context.
It extends `DataManagerContext` with specific data relevant to address operations,
such as geographical lookups.

@upmind-automation/headless!AddressModel.name: AddressModel
@upmind-automation/headless!AddressModel.tsdoc:
Interface representing the data model for an address, suitable for forms
or API payloads. It encapsulates the core geographical details of an address.

@upmind-automation/headless!AddressTypes.name: AddressTypes
@upmind-automation/headless!AddressTypes.tsdoc:
An array of predefined address types, used for categorising different kinds of addresses.
Each object contains a numeric `key` and a human-readable `value`.

@upmind-automation/headless!AllContextsF.name: AllContextsFromMatrix
@upmind-automation/headless!AllContextsF.tsdoc:
Helper type to extract ALL valid context types from a matrix.
Returns the union of all contexts across all concrete actors.
Used for SELF where the actual actor is unknown at compile time.

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthContext.name: AuthContext
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthContext.tsdoc: Context for the auth state machine.

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthContextT.name: AuthContextTypes
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthContextT.tsdoc:
Context types for auth module.
Defines what entities a staff member can authenticate on behalf of.

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthEvent.name: AuthEvent
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthEvent.tsdoc: Events that can be sent to the auth machine.

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthEvents.name: AuthEvents
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthEvents.tsdoc:
Interactive auth action that minted a token. Passed through `add()` /

subsequent-login `/self` cache-bust.

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthFlowType.name: AuthFlowTypes
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthFlowType.tsdoc:
Auth flows a client can start.

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthModel.name: AuthModel
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthModel.tsdoc: Union of all auth model types.

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthScopeMat.name: AuthScopeMatrix
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthScopeMat.tsdoc: Auth module context matrix type (derived from runtime const).

@upmind-automation/headless!AuthServices.name: AuthServices
@upmind-automation/headless!AuthServices.tsdoc: Auth services interface for actor-aware service implementations.

@upmind-automation/headless!Autocomplete.name: AutocompleteSuggestions
@upmind-automation/headless!Autocomplete.tsdoc:
Type alias for an array of Google Maps Autocomplete suggestions.
This is the raw type returned by the Google Places API for autocomplete queries.

@upmind-automation/headless!BasketContex.name: BasketContext
@upmind-automation/headless!BasketContex.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for the main shopping basket, typically managed by an XState machine.
It holds the entire state of the basket, including its products, summary, errors, and references
to spawned child actors for managing related concerns like billing, currency, and promotions.

@upmind-automation/headless!BasketHelper.name: BasketHelperContext
@upmind-automation/headless!BasketHelper.tsdoc:

@upmind-automation/headless!BasketOption.name: BasketOptionSummary
@upmind-automation/headless!BasketOption.tsdoc: A product summary detail with basket-specific toggle metadata.

@upmind-automation/headless!BasketProduc.name: BasketProduct

@upmind-automation/headless!BasketProduc.name: BasketProductInput

@upmind-automation/headless!Benefit.name: Benefit
@upmind-automation/headless!Benefit.tsdoc:

@upmind-automation/headless!BillingConte.name: BillingContext

@upmind-automation/headless!BillingCycle.name: BillingCycleFormats

@upmind-automation/headless!BillingModel.name: BillingModel

@upmind-automation/headless!DataLayerEco.name: DataLayerEcommerceItems
@upmind-automation/headless!DataLayerEco.tsdoc:
Interface representing a collection of e-commerce items, often used for add_to_cart, remove_from_cart,
or view_item_list events, which require currency and total value information.

@upmind-automation/headless!DataLayerPag.name: DataLayerPage
@upmind-automation/headless!DataLayerPag.tsdoc:
Interface representing page-specific data to be pushed to the data layer.
This helps track navigation, page views, and contextual information about the current page.

@upmind-automation/headless!DataLayerUse.name: DataLayerUser
@upmind-automation/headless!DataLayerUse.tsdoc:
Interface representing user-specific data to be pushed to the data layer.
This can include anonymised user IDs, login status, or other user attributes for analytics.

@upmind-automation/headless!DataProxy.name: DataProxy
@upmind-automation/headless!DataProxy.tsdoc:
Reactive proxy for data meta properties.

Unlike UIMetaProxy, data properties are simple types (booleans, strings, objects)
without value type enums, so no helpers are needed.
e.g., data.catalogueDisabled → false, data.categoryBadge → { label: "Popular" }

`-?` makes all properties required (removes optionality from DataSchema).

@upmind-automation/headless!DomainContex.name: DomainContext
@upmind-automation/headless!DomainContex.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for a basket helper, which facilitates
the conversion and management of products between a generic type `T` and
the specific `IBasketProduct` format required by the basket.

@upmind-automation/headless!DomainEnvelo.name: DomainEnvelopeResponse
@upmind-automation/headless!DomainEnvelo.tsdoc:
Domain-specific envelope returned by `/suggestions`, `/suggestions/tlds`
and `/availability/{domain}`. Narrows the loosely-typed `related` and
`meta` on the generic `QueryResponse` to the concrete shapes those
endpoints surface — `related.products` (product_id → `IProduct`) and
`meta.total_pages` — so domain callers read them off the raw envelope
via `useQuery().request(...)` without `as` casts.

@upmind-automation/headless!DomainMode.name: DomainMode
@upmind-automation/headless!DomainMode.tsdoc:
Enumeration defining the internal operation mode for the Domain Availability Checker (DAC).
This is distinct from DomainTypes which represents user-facing choices.

- `register`: runs suggestions + availability check (default search behaviour)
- `transfer`: skips suggestions, runs availability check + owned domain lookup only

@upmind-automation/headless!DomainModel.name: DomainModel
@upmind-automation/headless!DomainModel.tsdoc:
Represents the core data model for a domain name, including its parts and type.
This is used internally to manage the state of domains being processed.

@upmind-automation/headless!DomainProduc.name: DomainProduct
@upmind-automation/headless!DomainProduc.tsdoc:
Represents a Product specifically for domain management, augmented with domain-specific
meta-information like availability, ownership, and selection status.
It extends Product and omits `selected` from `DomainModel` to merge `meta`.

@upmind-automation/headless!DomainTypes.name: DomainTypes
@upmind-automation/headless!DomainTypes.tsdoc:
Enumeration defining the different types of domain management flows.
These types dictate the user interface, available actions, and underlying logic
for how a customer interacts with domain names, e.g. registering a new one,
transferring an existing one, or using one from their basket.

@upmind-automation/headless!Email.name: Email
@upmind-automation/headless!Email.tsdoc: An email address as read from the API, with its display and status fields.

@upmind-automation/headless!EmailContext.name: EmailContext
@upmind-automation/headless!EmailContext.tsdoc: The manager's machine context — the shared machine's, over this form model.

@upmind-automation/headless!EmailModel.name: EmailModel
@upmind-automation/headless!EmailModel.tsdoc: The form/request model for an email address.

@upmind-automation/headless!EmailTypes.name: EmailTypes
@upmind-automation/headless!EmailTypes.tsdoc: Predefined email categories, keyed by the API's `type` field.

@upmind-automation/headless!FormComposab.name: FormComposable
@upmind-automation/headless!FormComposab.tsdoc:
Interface representing the API of a generic form composable.
This contract defines common methods and properties expected from composables
that manage form state, data, and interactions, typically backed by an XState machine.

@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelContex.name: FunnelContext
@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelContex.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for the funnel, typically managed by an XState machine.
It holds the state of active flows, current route, and references to other services.

@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelMetaTa.name: FunnelMetaTarget
@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelMetaTa.tsdoc:
A single conditional navigation target.
Used in meta.next / meta.prev arrays for guard-based routing.

@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelStateM.name: FunnelStateMeta
@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelStateM.tsdoc:
Meta properties for funnel state nodes.
Used by the factory to auto-generate NEXT/BACK handlers (FE-2583).

`next` / `prev` accept either:
- A **string** — unconditional target (simple case).
- An **array of FunnelMetaTarget** — evaluated in order; first matching
  `cond` wins. Omit `cond` on the last entry for a default fallback.

@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelWatche.name: FunnelWatcher
@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelWatche.tsdoc:
A reactive watcher that subscribes to state changes and triggers
navigation through the funnel pipeline.

Must return a cleanup function (unsubscribe).
The watcher receives the funnel context for `resolved` mutex checking.

@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelWatche.name: FunnelWatcherHandler
@upmind-automation/headless!FunnelWatche.tsdoc:
Signature for the watcher handler function.
Sets up a reactive subscription and returns a cleanup function.
Must be self-contained — the handler manages its own lifecycle.

@upmind-automation/headless!GatewayAddPa.name: GatewayAddParams
@upmind-automation/headless!GatewayAddPa.tsdoc: Gateway parameters for ADD context — no orderId or amount needed.

@upmind-automation/headless!GatewayParam.name: GatewayParams
@upmind-automation/headless!GatewayParam.tsdoc:
Gateway parameters shared between PAY and ADD contexts.

`amount` and `orderId` are required for PAY context, optional for ADD.
Downstream gateway services access these without narrowing by `ctx`,
so they must remain accessible on the base type.

@upmind-automation/headless!GatewayPayPa.name: GatewayPayParams
@upmind-automation/headless!GatewayPayPa.tsdoc: Gateway parameters for PAY context — requires orderId and amount.

@upmind-automation/headless!GlobbedFiles.name: GlobbedFiles
@upmind-automation/headless!GlobbedFiles.tsdoc:
Type alias representing the structure of files loaded via a glob import
in a JavaScript/TypeScript module system (e.g. Vite's `import.meta.glob`).
This type is flexible to accommodate different glob import patterns,
either direct message objects or dynamic import functions.

@upmind-automation/headless!HasContexts.name: HasContexts
@upmind-automation/headless!HasContexts.tsdoc: Helper type to check if an actor has any valid contexts.

@upmind-automation/headless!IAuthTransfe.name: IAuthTransfer
@upmind-automation/headless!IAuthTransfe.tsdoc:
Interface representing the data for an authenticated session transfer.
This is used to securely transfer session context between different parts
of an application or between micro-frontends.

@upmind-automation/headless!IBasketProdu.name: IBasketProductModel
@upmind-automation/headless!IBasketProdu.tsdoc:
Interface representing the data model for a product when it's being added
to or configured within the shopping basket. It includes core product details
and optional configurations for attributes, options, provisioning, and promotions.

@upmind-automation/headless!IBasketSubpr.name: IBasketSubproductModel
@upmind-automation/headless!IBasketSubpr.tsdoc:
Interface representing the data model for a subproduct within a basket product.
This defines how subproducts (like add-ons or options) are structured when
being added or configured in the basket.

@upmind-automation/headless!IMessage.name: IMessage
@upmind-automation/headless!IMessage.tsdoc:
Interface representing a message object as typically retrieved from a backend API.
This includes unique identifiers, content, and translation metadata.

@upmind-automation/headless!IPhoneData.name: IPhoneData
@upmind-automation/headless!IPhoneData.tsdoc: Interface representing parsed phone number data, typically from a phone number parsing utility.

@upmind-automation/headless!IProductConf.name: IProductConfig
@upmind-automation/headless!IProductConf.tsdoc:
Interface representing raw product configuration properties, typically passed
from a backend API or extracted from URL parameters.

@upmind-automation/headless!Impersonatio.name: Impersonations
@upmind-automation/headless!Impersonatio.tsdoc:
Impersonation state for tracking parent session.
This is used to restore the "parent" session after impersonation.
The key being the impersonated actor ID and the value being the impersonator ( initiating actor) ID.

@upmind-automation/headless!InfiniteQuer.name: InfiniteQueryPage
@upmind-automation/headless!InfiniteQuer.tsdoc:
Represents the structure of a single page returned from an infinite query's `queryFn`.
This type is used internally by the `useInfiniteQuery` hook.

@upmind-automation/headless!Invoice.name: Invoice
@upmind-automation/headless!Invoice.tsdoc:
A billable invoice raised against an order — the client, currency, line
items, payment history, and amount/status summary.

@upmind-automation/headless!LabelContent.name: LabelContent
@upmind-automation/headless!LabelContent.tsdoc: Minimal labelled-content shape: a label, optionally annotated with an icon.

@upmind-automation/headless!LastPaymentM.name: LastPaymentModel
@upmind-automation/headless!LastPaymentM.tsdoc:
Persisted payment selections for retry/partial payment UX.
These values seed the paymentDetail machine on re-spawn
so the user sees their previous choices pre-filled.

@upmind-automation/headless!ListQuery.name: ListQuery
@upmind-automation/headless!ListQuery.tsdoc:
The `list()` query's return shape (`useQuery.ts`), parameterised by the raw
fetch type and the (optionally `select`-mapped) data type — mirrors
`list`'s own generic order/defaults. Extracted from `list`'s own inline
return-statement cast so a scoped module can express its list-query return
type without deriving `ReturnType<typeof localFn>` from its own
already-instantiated service function (graphify-out/ citation above — no
prior node for this type).

@upmind-automation/headless!LoadedSessio.name: LoadedSessionUsers
@upmind-automation/headless!LoadedSessio.tsdoc:
Result of loading `/self` for every session during boot resolution.
`users` holds the profiles that loaded; `invalidSessionIds` names the
sessions whose token returned `401` (dead token) and must be dropped so boot
falls through to the guest floor. A non-401 failure is a soft degrade and
appears in neither list.

@upmind-automation/headless!Locale.name: Locale
@upmind-automation/headless!Locale.tsdoc:
Interface representing a collection of loaded locale messages.
The keys are locale codes (e.g. "en-GB", "es"), and their values are
objects containing translation keys and their corresponding strings.

 Locale

@upmind-automation/headless!MatrixHasAny.name: MatrixHasAnyContexts
@upmind-automation/headless!MatrixHasAny.tsdoc:
Helper type to check if ANY actor in the matrix has valid contexts.
Used to determine if SELF should expose `.for()`.

@upmind-automation/headless!Message.name: Message
@upmind-automation/headless!Message.tsdoc:
Interface representing a client-side message object for display in the UI.
It contains content, display preferences, and optional actions.

@upmind-automation/headless!MessageError.name: MessageError
@upmind-automation/headless!MessageError.tsdoc:
Interface representing a structured error object, typically used for displaying
error messages from API responses or internal validation.

@upmind-automation/headless!MessageModel.name: MessageModel
@upmind-automation/headless!MessageModel.tsdoc:
Interface representing a client-side model for an IMessage,
simplifying the structure for UI consumption.

@upmind-automation/headless!MessagesCont.name: MessagesContext
@upmind-automation/headless!MessagesCont.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for a message management system,
typically managed by an XState machine. It holds references to active message actors.

@upmind-automation/headless!MetaInput.name: MetaInput
@upmind-automation/headless!MetaInput.tsdoc: Raw input for meta resolution (before reactive wrapper)

@upmind-automation/headless!MutationPara.name: MutationParams
@upmind-automation/headless!MutationPara.tsdoc:
Type alias defining parameters for TanStack Query's `useMutation` hook,
extending RequestParams with `MutationObserverOptions` and omitting `mutationFn`,
which is handled internally.

@upmind-automation/headless!MutationResu.name: MutationResult
@upmind-automation/headless!MutationResu.tsdoc:
The `mutate()` mutation's return shape (`useQuery.ts`), parameterised by
its resolved data type. Extracted from `mutate`'s own inline return-
statement cast for the same reason as ListQuery.

@upmind-automation/headless!OptionToggle.name: OptionToggleMeta
@upmind-automation/headless!OptionToggle.tsdoc: Toggle metadata for option switches in the basket.

@upmind-automation/headless!OrderContext.name: OrderContext
@upmind-automation/headless!OrderContext.tsdoc: Context for the order payment orchestrator machine.

@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayDefin.name: OverlayDefinition
@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayDefin.tsdoc: Definition for an overlay route that can be injected as a child on eligible routes.

@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayRegis.name: OverlayRegistry
@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayRegis.tsdoc: Overlay registry type — maps path suffix to route name

@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayRespo.name: OverlayResponse
@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayRespo.tsdoc:
Alternative guard payload (resolve/reject) for rendering an overlay over a
base route. The `setOverlay` action turns this into a `{base}--{overlayId}`
target, looking the overlay id up in the overlay registry. Funnel-agnostic —
`target` is the base FunnelTarget the overlay renders over (carrying any
params/query), `overlay` is the registered overlay route name.

@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayType.name: OverlayType
@upmind-automation/headless!OverlayType.tsdoc: Enumeration representing the UI container type for overlay routes.

@upmind-automation/headless!PAGINATION.name: PAGINATION
@upmind-automation/headless!PAGINATION.tsdoc:
Default pagination values for API requests.
These values can be used to standardise pagination across different requests.

@upmind-automation/headless!PERSONAL_DET.name: PERSONAL_DETAILS_SCOPE_MATRIX
@upmind-automation/headless!PERSONAL_DET.tsdoc:
Scope matrix shared by `usePersonalDetails` and `usePersonalDetailsManager`
(design.md §3.2 — a deliberate divergence from `client-email`'s two
matrices, since both composables here scope on the same entity). `client`
is the only actor that resolves; `staff` and `guest` are `null as never`,
which makes `.as('staff')` a compile-time error rather than an
advertised-but-absent capability.

@upmind-automation/headless!PageRoute.name: PageRoute
@upmind-automation/headless!PageRoute.tsdoc:
Interface representing details about a page route, typically including both the target route
and the route from which the navigation originated.

@upmind-automation/headless!PaginationIn.name: PaginationInfo
@upmind-automation/headless!PaginationIn.tsdoc:
Interface representing comprehensive pagination information, typically returned
by an API to describe the current state of paginated results.

@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentArgs.name: PaymentArgs
@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentArgs.tsdoc:
Interface representing the arguments required to initiate a payment.
These details are essential for processing a transaction.

@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentConte.name: PaymentContext
@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentConte.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for a payment operation, typically managed by an XState machine.
It extends PaymentArgs with additional details for handling payment cancellations,
approvals, and tracking the payment attempt itself.

@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentDetai.name: PaymentDetailsArgs
@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentDetai.tsdoc:
Arguments required to initialise payment details context.
These details provide the necessary context for payment forms and gateway interactions.

For PAY context: orderId, orderStatus, and amount are required.
For ADD context: these are not needed (storing a payment method independently).

@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentDetai.name: PaymentDetailsContext
@upmind-automation/headless!PaymentDetai.tsdoc:
Context for payment details management, used by the XState machine.
Extends PaymentDetailsArgs with properties for handling
available gateways, payment types, stored methods, wallet balance, form schemas, and error states.

Supports both PAY and ADD contexts via the `ctx` property.

@upmind-automation/headless!PendingOpera.name: PendingOperation
@upmind-automation/headless!PendingOpera.tsdoc:
Shape of a pending ADD operation stored in sessionStorage.
Used for off-site redirect recovery (e.g. 3DS / SCA).

@upmind-automation/headless!PersistedSes.name: PersistedSessionState
@upmind-automation/headless!PersistedSes.tsdoc:
Shape persisted to sessionStorage.
Contains all session data needed to fully restore the store on page reload.
Excludes transient flags (`initialised`, `loading`) which reset on each load.

@upmind-automation/headless!PersonalDeta.name: PersonalDetailsScopeMatrix
@upmind-automation/headless!PersonalDeta.tsdoc: Scope matrix type, shared by both composables (derived from the runtime const).

@upmind-automation/headless!Phone.name: Phone
@upmind-automation/headless!Phone.tsdoc:
Interface representing a comprehensive phone object, extending PhoneModel
with additional identifiers, computed display fields, and meta-data about its status.
This is typically used for phone numbers retrieved from the API or displayed in the UI.

@upmind-automation/headless!PhoneContext.name: PhoneContext
@upmind-automation/headless!PhoneContext.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for phone number management within a client item context.
It extends `DataManagerContext` with specific data relevant to phone operations,
such as geographical country context for phone number formatting and validation.

@upmind-automation/headless!PhoneModel.name: PhoneModel
@upmind-automation/headless!PhoneModel.tsdoc:
Interface representing the data model for a phone number, suitable for forms
or API payloads.

@upmind-automation/headless!Place.name: Place
@upmind-automation/headless!Place.tsdoc:
Represents a geographical place with basic identification and address details.
This structure is used for displaying search results or selected locations.

@upmind-automation/headless!PlacePredict.name: PlacePrediction
@upmind-automation/headless!PlacePredict.tsdoc:
Type alias representing a simplified place prediction object, extracted from
Google Maps Place Prediction results for easier display in UI components.

@upmind-automation/headless!PlacePredict.name: PlacePredictions
@upmind-automation/headless!PlacePredict.tsdoc:
Type alias for an array of Google Maps Place Prediction objects.
These are the results returned from a Google Places Autocomplete request.

@upmind-automation/headless!PlaceService.name: PlaceService
@upmind-automation/headless!PlaceService.tsdoc:
Type alias representing the structure of the Google Maps Places service object,
providing access to core classes and constructors for Places API functionality.
This allows for instantiation of Google Maps Places objects within the application.

@upmind-automation/headless!Price.name: Price
@upmind-automation/headless!Price.tsdoc: The price details for any price, allowing for gross/net and discount breakdowns.

@upmind-automation/headless!PriceDetail.name: PriceDetail
@upmind-automation/headless!PriceDetail.tsdoc:
The full price details for any product or item displayed in the UI.
This type extends PriceDisplay and provides additional breakdowns
for display and tracking purposes, including individual unit prices (gross and net)
and the total configuration price (gross and net).

@upmind-automation/headless!PriceDisplay.name: PriceDisplay
@upmind-automation/headless!PriceDisplay.tsdoc:
The display price structure for any price that is shown in the UI.
This structure always provides full price details based on the total configuration,
which may be gross or net depending on brand settings. It includes quantity modifiers,
discounts, and any other adjustments. Essentially, this is the final price that
should be presented to the customer.

@upmind-automation/headless!PriceEntry.name: PriceEntry
@upmind-automation/headless!PriceEntry.tsdoc: Type alias for displaying price calculation states.

@upmind-automation/headless!Product.name: Product
@upmind-automation/headless!Product.tsdoc:
Represents a "configured" product with its configuration, pricing, and associated details.
This type aggregates all information necessary for displaying and managing a product
in various contexts, such as a product page or shopping basket.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBread.name: ProductBreadcrumb
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBread.tsdoc: Type alias for a product breadcrumb item, used for navigational paths.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBundl.name: ProductBundle
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBundl.tsdoc: Interface representing a product bundle, extending IRelatedObject.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBundl.name: ProductBundleConfig
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBundl.tsdoc:
Configuration for a product bundle item.
Used in `@data.productsToBundle` to define products that should be automatically added.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBundl.name: ProductBundles
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductBundl.tsdoc: Type alias for a collection of product bundles.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductConfi.name: ProductConfigContext
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductConfi.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for product configuration, typically managed by an XState machine.
It holds the state for configuring a single product, including its model, lookups, pricing, and associated errors.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductDetai.name: ProductDetails
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductDetai.tsdoc:
Represents the actual store product details, typically retrieved from the API.
This contains all the displayable and configurable information for a product.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductImage.name: ProductImage
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductImage.tsdoc: Type alias for a product image.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductModel.name: ProductModel
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductModel.tsdoc:
Represents the product model used for configuration, which is built and verified by a schema.
This is the core data structure for configuring a product's attributes, options, and provision fields.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductProps.name: ProductProps
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductProps.tsdoc:
Interface defining the properties required to create or configure a product.
It extends ProductModel with additional client, currency, and promotion details.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductRecom.name: ProductRecommendConfig
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductRecom.tsdoc:
Configuration for a product recommendation item.
Used in `@data.productsToRecommend` to define cross-sell recommendations.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductRecom.name: ProductRecommendConfigOptions
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductRecom.tsdoc:
Configuration options for a product recommendation.
Defines quantity, billing cycle, subproducts, provision fields, and coupons.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSorta.name: ProductSortableProperties
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSorta.tsdoc: Properties by which products can be sorted.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.name: ProductSummary
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.tsdoc: Type alias for a product summary, aggregating key pricing and detail information.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.name: ProductSummaryDetail
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.tsdoc: Type alias for a product summary detail, providing name, title, cycle, and meta-information.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.name: ProductSummaryDetailWithPrice
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.tsdoc: Type alias for a product summary detail that also includes pricing information.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.name: ProductSummaryMeta
@upmind-automation/headless!ProductSumma.tsdoc: Type alias for meta-information about a product summary.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileConte.name: ProfileContext
@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileConte.tsdoc:
The manager's machine context — the shared machine's, over this form
model. Was `FieldsContext` — renamed to resolve its collision with
`basket-fields.types.ts:11` (design.md §0). `lookups.fields` /
`.filterFields` / `.languages` are read via the generic `lookups?: Record<string, any[]>`
DataManagerContext already declares — never widened here, matching
`EmailContext = DataManagerContext<EmailModel>`'s own precedent.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileField.name: ProfileField
@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileField.tsdoc: One profile field projected for display — native or custom.

@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileModel.name: ProfileModel
@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileModel.tsdoc:
The form/request model for the profile editor. Was `FieldsModel` — renamed
to resolve its collision with `basket-fields.types.ts:6` (design.md §0).

@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileRecor.name: ProfileRecord
@upmind-automation/headless!ProfileRecor.tsdoc:
The client's profile as read off the wire — native fields plus the raw
embedded custom field values (each carrying its own definition, AC-16).
`mapProfile` produces this; `mapProfileFields` projects it for display.

@upmind-automation/headless!PromotionDet.name: PromotionDetails
@upmind-automation/headless!PromotionDet.tsdoc: Type alias for detailed information about a promotion.

@upmind-automation/headless!PromotionMod.name: PromotionModel
@upmind-automation/headless!PromotionMod.tsdoc: Type alias for a promotion model, containing the promotion code.

@upmind-automation/headless!PropertyDefi.name: PropertyDefinition
@upmind-automation/headless!PropertyDefi.tsdoc: Definition for a single meta property (from schema)

@upmind-automation/headless!QueryParams.name: QueryParams
@upmind-automation/headless!QueryParams.tsdoc:
Type alias defining parameters for TanStack Query's `useQuery` hook,
extending RequestParams with `QueryObserverOptions` and omitting
`queryFn` and `initialData`, which are handled internally.

@upmind-automation/headless!QueryProps.name: QueryProps
@upmind-automation/headless!QueryProps.tsdoc: Type alias defining common properties for API queries, including sorting, filtering, and pagination.

@upmind-automation/headless!QueryRespons.name: QueryResponse
@upmind-automation/headless!QueryRespons.tsdoc:
Interface representing a standardised response structure from an API query.
It encapsulates the status, data, total count, error, and messages.

@upmind-automation/headless!QueryRespons.name: QueryResponseError
@upmind-automation/headless!QueryRespons.tsdoc: Interface representing a structured error response from an API query.

@upmind-automation/headless!REQUIRES_ACT.name: REQUIRES_ACTION
@upmind-automation/headless!REQUIRES_ACT.tsdoc:
Enumeration representing various states or conditions that may require an action to be taken by the user or system.
This is often used in contexts like product configuration, order validation, or resource management.

@upmind-automation/headless!REQUIRES_SET.name: REQUIRES_SETUP
@upmind-automation/headless!REQUIRES_SET.tsdoc: Enumeration representing conditions that require product setup.

@upmind-automation/headless!ReactiveQuer.name: ReactiveQueryKeys
@upmind-automation/headless!ReactiveQuer.tsdoc:
Type alias for reactive query keys used to create dynamic query keys for TanStack Query.
This allows query keys to automatically update based on reactive sources.

@upmind-automation/headless!RecaptchaCon.name: RecaptchaContext
@upmind-automation/headless!RecaptchaCon.tsdoc:
Interface representing the context for Google reCAPTCHA integration,
typically managed by an XState machine. It holds the reCAPTCHA site key,

@upmind-automation/headless!authSubscrip.name: authSubscription
@upmind-automation/headless!authSubscrip.tsdoc:
Auth subscription helper for XState machines.
Spawned as a callback actor, emits events to the parent machine:

- SESSION: A new active session was set (guest, client, or staff).
  Fires any time the active session token changes.
- AUTHENTICATED: Transitioned from unauthenticated → authenticated (login).
- UNAUTHENTICATED: Transitioned from authenticated → unauthenticated (logout).

Auth events are emitted BEFORE session events so machines can
clean up state (e.g. clear basket on logout) before reloading
with the new session.

Uses raw TanStack store subscription (not Vue watch) so it works
inside XState's spawn() context which runs outside Vue's effect scope.

Fires an initial callback on creation: SESSION if a session exists,
AUTHENTICATED if authenticated. Never fires UNAUTHENTICATED on initial.

@upmind-automation/headless!isAbortError.tsdoc:
Detects whether a caught query-layer rejection represents an aborted
request rather than a real error.

`doFetch` rejects aborts with bare `undefined` (see
`query/services.ts:75`), so a `.code === responseCodes.Aborted` check
never fires for the common abort path — `undefined?.code` is undefined.
This helper covers four shapes that can reach a downstream
`.catch(error)` handler (or `doFetch`'s own pre-classification):
  1. `undefined` — `doFetch`'s `Promise.reject()` with no value. Note:
     `null` is intentionally NOT treated as an abort; callers that
     reject with `null` for a non-abort reason should surface that
     error rather than have it silently swallowed.
  2. `{ name: "AbortError" }` — native fetch `AbortError` if it ever
     slips past the `doFetch` catch (defensive).
  3. `{ code: responseCodes.Aborted }` — structured shape for any
     caller that explicitly rejects with the canonical aborted code.
  4. `{ status: responseCodes.Aborted }` — fetch-response-shape used
     inside `doFetch`'s own catch to classify before re-rejecting.

@upmind-automation/headless!useClientRec.name: useClientReceivedEmail
@upmind-automation/headless!useClientRec.tsdoc:
Composable function for managing client phones.
It handles fetching, displaying, filtering, and performing actions on client phones,
leveraging an underlying service and TanStack Query for data management.

@upmind-automation/headless!useClientRec.name: useClientReceivedEmails
@upmind-automation/headless!useClientRec.tsdoc:
Composable function for managing client emails.
It handles fetching, displaying, filtering, and performing actions on client emails,
leveraging an underlying service and TanStack Query for data management.

@upmind-automation/headless!useClientSlo.name: useClientSlots
@upmind-automation/headless!useClientSlo.tsdoc:
Composable function to provide reactive state and methods to manage and interact with client area templates (slots).
This includes state management for query meta-information, error handling, data retrieval,
and operational methods such as fetching and invalidating data.

@upmind-automation/headless!useClientTem.name: useClientTemplate
@upmind-automation/headless!useClientTem.tsdoc:
Composable function to manage the query, the state, and the context for client area templates.
Allows fetching, monitoring, and refreshing the data for client area templates.

@upmind-automation/headless!useDac.name: useDac
@upmind-automation/headless!useDac.tsdoc:
Composable for managing domain selection and search logic using XState and Vue.
Provides state, context, and helpers for domain-related flows (DAC, existing, basket).

@upmind-automation/headless!useDataLayer.name: useDataLayer
@upmind-automation/headless!useDataLayer.tsdoc: Composable for managing the data layer for tracking and analytics.

@upmind-automation/headless!useDomain.name: useDomain
@upmind-automation/headless!useDomain.tsdoc:
Composable for managing domain selection and search logic using XState and Vue.
Provides state, context, and helpers for domain-related flows (DAC, existing, basket).

@upmind-automation/headless!useDomainPar.name: useDomainParser
@upmind-automation/headless!useDomainPar.tsdoc:
Reactive domain parser — sanitises a raw domain input into its component
parts (full domain, SLD, TLD).

@upmind-automation/headless!useFeedback.name: useFeedback
@upmind-automation/headless!useFeedback.tsdoc:
Composable function to manage feedback messages using an XState state machine.
Provides methods for adding, dismissing, and displaying different types of messages
such as errors, successes, warnings, and system notifications.
This uses a global instance of the feedback machine.

@upmind-automation/headless!useI18n.name: useI18n
@upmind-automation/headless!useI18n.signature: useI18n(): Composer<object, object, object, string, never, string> & object
@upmind-automation/headless!useI18n.tsdoc:
Composable function to provide functionality for initialising and managing internationalisation (i18n) in an application.
The `useI18n` variable offers methods to configure the i18n instance, load locale messages, and set the active locale.

@upmind-automation/headless!useInvalidPr.name: useInvalidProductConfigSchema
@upmind-automation/headless!useInvalidPr.tsdoc:
Generates a JSON Schema containing only properties with validation errors.
Used to strip a model down to only the invalid fields via useModelParser.

@upmind-automation/headless!useInvalidPr.name: useInvalidProductConfigUischema
@upmind-automation/headless!useInvalidPr.tsdoc:
Builds a UISchema containing only elements that need attention.

This mirrors `useProductConfigUischema` but only includes elements where the
corresponding field has an error, or (when mode is 'deferred') where deferred
provision fields have empty values.

@upmind-automation/headless!useInvoice.name: useInvoice
@upmind-automation/headless!useInvoice.tsdoc:
Composable function to manage the state and data for a single invoice.
Provides methods to load, access, and invalidate invoice data.

@upmind-automation/headless!useLocale.name: useLocale
@upmind-automation/headless!useLocale.tsdoc:
Composable function to provide locale-related utilities and state management for internationalisation (i18n).

This module is responsible for controlling and updating the current locale, determining supported languages,
and applying fallback logic for selecting appropriate locales based on user or system preferences.

Note: Changing the locale is restricted while the user is authenticated to prevent inconsistencies, as
the locale is tied to the account's preferred language.

@upmind-automation/headless!useLocalisat.name: useLocalisation
@upmind-automation/headless!useLocalisat.signature: useLocalisation(instance: I18n<object, object, object, string, boolean>, glob: GlobbedFiles): object
@upmind-automation/headless!useLocalisat.tsdoc:
Composable function to manage and initialise localisation settings in headless with an associated i18n instance and optionally globbed messages.
Provides utilities to configure, load locale messages, and manage the application's locale state.

@upmind-automation/headless!useMessage.name: useMessage
@upmind-automation/headless!useMessage.tsdoc:
Extracts the message from an actor item.
It is used to simplify the extraction of message properties from the feedback machine.

@upmind-automation/headless!useOrder.name: useOrder
@upmind-automation/headless!useOrder.tsdoc:
Composable that orchestrates invoice payment via the order machine.
Spawns paymentDetailMachine as a child actor, invokes paymentMachine for
processing, and supports retry and partial payment loops.

@upmind-automation/headless!usePayment.name: usePayment
@upmind-automation/headless!usePayment.tsdoc:
A composable function that manages payment state, context, and actions using a state machine
implementation. Provides tools for orchestrating payment flow, including
meta-information, error handling, and event triggers like pay and refresh.

@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentDe.name: usePaymentDetail
@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentDe.signature: usePaymentDetail(service: ActorRef<any, any> | ComputedRef<UseActor | undefined>): object
@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentDe.tsdoc:
A composable function that provides access to the payment gateway actor.
in the PAY context

@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentDe.name: usePaymentDetails
@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentDe.tsdoc:
Composable to manage the stored payment details.
It provides methods to retrieve stored payment details.

@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentGa.name: usePaymentGateway
@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentGa.signature: usePaymentGateway(service: ActorRef<any, any> | ComputedRef<UseActor | undefined>): object
@upmind-automation/headless!usePaymentGa.tsdoc: A composable function that provides access to the payment gateway actor.

@upmind-automation/headless!usePersonalD.name: usePersonalDetails
@upmind-automation/headless!usePersonalD.tsdoc: Scoped composable for reading a client's own profile.

@upmind-automation/headless!usePersonalD.name: usePersonalDetailsManager
@upmind-automation/headless!usePersonalD.tsdoc:
Scoped composable for editing a client's own profile. Callable bare
(AC-43) — `usePersonalDetailsManager().as('client')` constructs and
settles without a caller-supplied option.

@upmind-automation/headless!usePlaces.name: usePlaces
@upmind-automation/headless!usePlaces.tsdoc:
Composable function to provide utility methods and state for integrating with
the Google Places API. It initialises the Places API, manages its readiness state,
and offers features for searching address predictions, retrieving place details,
and accessing prediction results.

@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCa.name: useProductCatalogue
@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCa.tsdoc:
A composable function that manages the product catalogue.
It provides methods to filter, sort, and retrieve products from the catalogue.

@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCa.name: useProductCategories
@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCa.tsdoc:
A composable function that manages and interacts with product categories.
Provides reactive state and utilities for handling hierarchical category structures.
The primary use case is to interact with category data via query operations.

@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCo.name: useProductConfig
@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCo.tsdoc:
A composable function that provides functionality and state management for product configuration.
It integrates various aspects of product customisation, such as quantity, terms, attributes, and options,
while managing the underlying state using an actor-based state management system.

@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCo.name: useProductConfigSchema
@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCo.tsdoc:
Builds a JSON schema from the current product lookups.

Each section (term, options, attributes, provision fields) becomes a property
on the root schema object. The schema is the single source of truth for
validation — `required` arrays, `minProperties`, `oneOf` constraints etc.

@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCo.name: useProductConfigUischema
@upmind-automation/headless!useProductCo.tsdoc:
Builds a UI schema that drives the layout of the unified product config form.

Custom `type` values (`Terms`, `SubProducts`) are matched by the
corresponding renderers via `uiTypeIs()` testers. Provision fields use
standard `Control` elements handled by existing renderers.

Display data (terms array, subproduct details) is passed via `options`
spread flat — NOT nested under a key. `title`/`description` stay in the
JSON schema (standard properties), everything else goes here.

@upmind-automation/headless!useProductRe.name: useProductRecommendations
@upmind-automation/headless!useProductRe.tsdoc:
A composable function that manages the product recommendations
for a specific product. It uses the recommendation engine
to fetch and manage the recommendations.
NB: Only recommendations that originate from the specified product will be available.
This is useful for displaying recommendations on the product detail page, or after adding to the basket

@upmind-automation/headless!useQuery.name: useQuery
@upmind-automation/headless!useQuery.tsdoc:
A composable function that provides utilities for making HTTP requests
with advanced functionalities like pagination, sorting, filtering, currency handling,
and caching using TanStack Query. It provides methods for sending requests and handling
responses in a reactive way.

@upmind-automation/headless!useQueryPara.name: useQueryParams
@upmind-automation/headless!useQueryPara.tsdoc:
Composable function to manage query parameters from a specified or current route.

The `useQueryParams` function retrieves the query parameters for a given route.
If no route is provided, the function will default to using the current route.
It ensures that the route object has safe defaults for its properties
including `name`, `path`, `query`, and `params`.

@upmind-automation/headless!useRecaptcha.name: useRecaptcha
@upmind-automation/headless!useRecaptcha.tsdoc:
Composable function to provide functionality for managing reCAPTCHA services.
It includes methods for initialising, generating tokens, checking readiness, and handling reCAPTCHA state.

@upmind-automation/headless!useRecommend.name: useRecommendations
@upmind-automation/headless!useRecommend.tsdoc:
A composable function that manages recommendations engine functionalities.

This hook initialises and interacts with the recommendation engine service
and provides access to its state, context, and operations.

@upmind-automation/headless!useRegisterS.name: useRegisterSchema
@upmind-automation/headless!useRegisterS.tsdoc:
JSON Schema for the registration form.
Includes custom fields from brand configuration.

@upmind-automation/headless!useRegisterU.name: useRegisterUischema
@upmind-automation/headless!useRegisterU.tsdoc: UI Schema for the registration form.

@upmind-automation/headless!useRoutingEn.name: useRoutingEngine
@upmind-automation/headless!useRoutingEn.tsdoc:
Composable function to provide a routing engine to handle route management, navigation, and state control within the application.

This composable enables integration with internationalisation, session, and basket states, and allows for advanced
route resolution and flow management.

@upmind-automation/headless!useSessionSt.name: useSessionStore
@upmind-automation/headless!useSessionSt.tsdoc:
Composable for accessing the multi-session store.
Supports multiple simultaneous sessions per actor type (guest, client, staff).

**Important:** Call `initialise()` from `useUpmind` before using other sub-composables.
This ensures config (allowedScopes) is set before state is built.

@upmind-automation/headless!useSystem.name: useSystem
@upmind-automation/headless!useSystem.tsdoc:
The `useSystem` composable provides a simple interface to interact with the system API
and includes utility methods for fetching data.

@upmind-automation/headless!useTermsAndC.name: useTermsAndConditions
@upmind-automation/headless!useTermsAndC.tsdoc: Composable to get the current terms and conditions.

@upmind-automation/headless!useTheming.name: useTheming
@upmind-automation/headless!useTheming.tsdoc: Composable for consolidating brand theme information with any provided themes through the upmind initialisation

@upmind-automation/headless!useTracking.name: useTracking
@upmind-automation/headless!useTracking.tsdoc:
Composable function to handle user tracking data. The `useTracking` hook provides mechanisms for initialising,
retrieving, and managing tracking data from cookies. This may include generating and storing
tracking data based on query parameters and providing methods to retrieve or clear this data.

Note that the composable relies on external libraries and configurations such as cookies and URL handling.

@upmind-automation/headless!useTransfer.name: useTransfer
@upmind-automation/headless!useTransfer.tsdoc:
Composable for session transfer functionality.
Provides methods to generate and consume transfer codes for cross-domain/tab session sharing.

@upmind-automation/headless!useUpload.name: useUpload
@upmind-automation/headless!useUpload.tsdoc:
Composable function to manage file uploads, providing state, context, and methods
for handling the upload process.

NB: System uploads are NOT a global instance and are always instantiated as a new machine
this is because we need to be able to have multiple uploads happening at once,
and we need to be able to start and stop them individually

@upmind-automation/headless!validateMeta.name: validateMeta
@upmind-automation/headless!validateMeta.tsdoc:
Validates a meta object's conditional rules without throwing.

Walks each setting and checks rule shape, state key/operator/operand types,
and per-context availability. Returns a list of issues at error/warning/info
severity for callers to surface in editors or logs.
